examples.title: A turn of 30 calls
examples.description: The first 3 and last 3 calls stay on the rail around one dashed "Show 24 more" button that says what it hides, counted from this turn only. The failed Send email keeps its danger line with Details, Ask the agent to retry and Copy input, and the call waiting on you stays its own row with its approval beneath it. Choosing a row selects it; "Show 24 more" opens the hidden calls in place and "Show fewer" folds them again.

examples.title: Collapsed to one line
examples.description: Closed, the rail shows only the summary line "Used 30 tools · 1 failed · 1 waiting on you · 18s" with its chevron pointing right. The call that failed and the call waiting on you stay under it, with the failure line, its links and the approval, so nothing that needs a person is ever folded away.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { ApprovalCard, ToolCallRail } from '@lostgradient/cinder';
  import type { ToolCallRailCall } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const filler = Array.from({ length: 27 }, (_, index): ToolCallRailCall => ({
    id: `done-${index}`,
    name: index % 3 === 0 ? 'Search orders' : 'Lookup order',
    input: String(4400 + index),
    result: 'found',
    duration: '0.3s',
    status: 'done',
  }));
  const calls: ToolCallRailCall[] = [
    ...filler,
    {
      id: 'send-email',
      name: 'Send email',
      identifier: 'send-email',
      input: 'maya@example.com',
      result: 'SMTP timeout after 10s',
      duration: '10.0s',
      status: 'failed',
      failure: "Mail server didn't reply within 10s. The refund notice for 4471 wasn't sent.",
    },
    {
      id: 'refund-4476',
      name: 'Issue refund',
      input: '4476, $96.00',
      result: 'Approved by you 9:58 AM',
      duration: '0.9s',
      status: 'done',
    },
    {
      id: 'refund-4480',
      name: 'Issue refund',
      identifier: 'issue-refund',
      input: '4480, $27.25',
      status: 'waiting',
      nested: true,
    },
  ];
</script>

<ToolCallRail
  {calls}
  open={false}
  duration="18s"
  onSelect={() => undefined}
  onRetry={() => undefined}
  onCopyInput={() => undefined}
>
  {#snippet children()}
    <ApprovalCard
      layout="row"
      tool={{ name: 'issue-refund', label: 'Issue refund', risk: 'high', irreversible: true }}
      question="Refund order 4480 for $27.25?"
      source="the agent"
      requestedAt={new Date(Date.now() - 2 * 60_000).toISOString()}
      consequence="Sends $27.25 back to the original card"
      operation={{
        kind: 'other',
        argsPreview: { orderId: '4480', amount: '$27.25', reason: 'Arrived damaged' },
      }}
      policyVersion="policy-2026-11"
      idempotencyKey="approval-4480-collapsed"
      state="pending"
      onResolve={() => undefined}
    />
  {/snippet}
</ToolCallRail>

examples.title: Still running
examples.description: While the turn runs the summary reads "Used 12 tools so far…" with a spinner and no failed or waiting counts. The rail keeps the first 3 calls, one dashed "Show 8 more" button and the call under way, which shows a spinner in place of the dot, "Running…" in place of a result and the elapsed time. A second rail shows a short turn whose last call is still running.

examples.title: A denied call
examples.description: A call a person refused reads Denied, in neutral text with a prohibition glyph: it is not called Failed and carries no error block. The words are the caller's ("Denied by you 10:40 AM · nothing refunded"), and a denied call never folds away.

examples.title: A failure inside the hidden run
examples.description: A failure in the middle of a run stays on the rail between two folded groups: the first 3 calls, "Show 10 more · 10 done: Lookup order ×10", the failed Send email with its danger line and links, "Show 13 more · 13 done: Check inventory ×4, Lookup customer ×4, Search orders ×3, 2 others", then the last 3 calls. Each group counts only the calls it hides.
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { ToolCallRail } from '@lostgradient/cinder';
  import type { ToolCallRailCall } from '@lostgradient/cinder';

  const done = (
    id: string,
    name: string,
    input: string,
    result: string,
    duration = '0.3s',
  ): ToolCallRailCall => ({ id, name, input, result, duration, status: 'done' });

  const calls: ToolCallRailCall[] = [
    done('f1', 'Search orders', 'carrier Parcelly, damaged', '14 orders', '0.6s'),
    done('f2', 'Lookup order', '4471', '$42.00, delivered Mon', '0.2s'),
    done('f3', 'Lookup order', '4476', '$96.00, delivered Mon'),
    ...Array.from({ length: 10 }, (_, index) =>
      done(`lookup-${index}`, 'Lookup order', String(4480 + index), '$20.00'),
    ),
    {
      id: 'send-email',
      name: 'Send email',
      identifier: 'send-email',
      input: 'maya@example.com',
      result: 'SMTP timeout after 10s',
      duration: '10.0s',
      status: 'failed',
      failure: "Mail server didn't reply within 10s. The refund notice for 4471 wasn't sent.",
    },
    ...Array.from({ length: 4 }, (_, index) =>
      done(`stock-${index}`, 'Check inventory', `MUG-0${index}`, `${index + 3} in stock`),
    ),
    ...Array.from({ length: 4 }, (_, index) =>
      done(`customer-${index}`, 'Lookup customer', `cus_${index}`, 'Found'),
    ),
    ...Array.from({ length: 3 }, (_, index) =>
      done(`search-${index}`, 'Search orders', `prior refunds ${index}`, 'none'),
    ),
    done('policy', 'Read policy', 'refund-policy', 'Damaged items refundable'),
    done('ticket-1', 'Update ticket', 'T-2290', 'Marked pending refund'),
    done('draft-1', 'Draft email', 'refund notice, 4471', 'Draft saved', '0.6s'),
    done('draft-2', 'Draft email', 'refund notice, 4472', 'Draft saved', '0.6s'),
    done('ticket-2', 'Update ticket', 'T-2291', 'Marked pending refund'),
  ];
</script>

<ToolCallRail
  {calls}
  duration="21s"
  onSelect={() => undefined}
  onRetry={() => undefined}
  onCopyInput={() => undefined}
/>

examples.title: Short turns and where the fold starts
examples.description: One or two calls are plain rows: no "Used N tools" line, no rail and no fold. From 3 calls the summary line appears and every call still shows. From 8 calls the middle folds, with the first 3 and last 3 around "Show 2 more · 2 done: Lookup order ×2". With 7 calls hiding one row would save nothing, so all 7 show.

examples.title: A turn that ends on a tool call
examples.description: A finished turn whose last step is a tool call closes the rail with the run's end state, "Run finished · no reply", on its own line with a check glyph, so the turn does not look hung. A call a person approved has a green dot ("Approved by you 10:33 AM · $18.50 refunded").
examples.code:
<script lang="ts">
  import { ToolCallRail } from '@lostgradient/cinder';
</script>

<ToolCallRail
  calls={[
    {
      id: 'lookup',
      name: 'Lookup order',
      identifier: 'lookup-order',
      input: '4472',
      result: '$18.50, delivered Oct 29, flagged damaged',
      duration: '0.3s',
      status: 'done',
    },
    {
      id: 'refund',
      name: 'Issue refund',
      identifier: 'issue-refund',
      input: '4472',
      result: 'Approved by you 10:33 AM · $18.50 refunded',
      duration: '0.6s',
      status: 'approved',
    },
  ]}
  endLabel="Run finished · no reply"
/>

examples.title: An approved call with its approval beneath it
examples.description: A tool that changes things is one rail row with its approval nested under it, drawn as decided: "Approved by you · 10:42 AM" shows once, on the nested approval, and the row itself carries the result.

examples.title: The selected row
examples.description: The row whose panel is open is tinted and keeps the shared quiet focus ring, 2px and wrapping the whole row, while its panel is open. Choosing it again closes the panel; Esc or Close in the panel hands focus back to that row through focusCall.

examples.title: At 375 px
examples.description: In a narrow container each row has two lines: the name and duration on line one, and a muted line of key input and result, cut with an ellipsis, on line two. The summary reads "Used 30 tools · 1 failed · 1 waiting on you" with no duration, the dashed button says "Show 24 more" with the short "24 done", the failed row is red with a red cross and the waiting row is amber. The approval nests under the waiting row, and the failure line gives way to the panel.
